title: Using Frontier Models - Which engine, if any, are people using?
author: MKBSP
selftext:
I'm curious, I see all these games, some spent $100's other much less, greatly varying in quality and output, and a surprising number of people post their games with 0 insight into the stack, engine, workflow, etc.. 

Thank you

comments.author: sirpalee
comments.body:
Most common is threejs. There is tons of javascript / typescript code put there, so agents are good at it, and threejs is a very popular javascript library.

Threejs is mostly about rendering, but you don't really need an engine if you can generate code at a breakneck pace.

replies.author: derAres
replies.body: I started using Unreal Engine to build a shooter. Do you think I‘d be faster by just putting code together and not using an engine? Three.js is nice and i did quite a few games in it, but I want to move past the browser.

replies.author: sirpalee
replies.body:
That depends heavily on your experience, your goals for the game, the type of game you are making, the platforms you are targeting, and so on. So can't really answer.

If you mostly use agents to engineer your code, some engine that is not built around having an editor is going to make your life easier.

replies.author: derAres
replies.body: Unreal has the api for claude now. It made me a shooter overnight and I haven‘t touched the gui. But it „feels“ a bit slow. I did the same shooter in three.js a few days ago and it seemed way quicker and as of now it even feels better. But graphics are a factor.

replies.author: Sencha-Games
replies.body:
You should honestly just use an engine.

Unreal Engine might be overkill for a shooter if you're not aiming for photorealism. If I were you, I'd ask Claude to fork the Quake 2 or Quake 3 engine (or a sourceport) and mod it to your needs.

I'd shill my own game engine but it's not done yet :) One day I'll be annoying about it and tell people they should have used the Sencha Engine to make their dream game lmao

replies.author: MKBSP
replies.body: Thank you man, I'm familiar with threejs, but not ever considered it for gamedev.
